answer: Summed social capital — defined as the Z-scored Copper&Gold (ZCU_AU) + Amber (Zamber) + Monument Count (ZMonument) — peaked in the 14th–13th centuries BCE, with the exact maximum (sum = 4.24 Z-units) reached at BCE 1400 and BCE 1300 (the tied maximum spans BCE 1400–1300); the nearest non-adjacent values (BCE 1100–1200, 3.62) are ~0.6 units lower, so this late-Bronze-Age peak is unambiguous. At the peak the components that increase are Copper & Gold (value +2.54, above its long-run mean ~0 and only slightly below its all-period record of 2.85 at BCE 1100–1200) and Monument Count (+1.71, above its long-run mean ~0 and rising by +0.36 versus the preceding century, second only to its early peak at BCE 2700). Amber (~-0.01) is NOT an increasing component at this peak: it sits at its period average, far below its own early-Neolithic maximum (~BCE 3000–3300), so the late-Bronze-Age social-capital peak is driven specifically by the joint surge in copper/gold and monument count, not by amber. Robustness: (i) the independent interpolated 1-year time-series (century means) confirms the same 14th–13th-century-BCE window, with the 14th century BCE as the top century-mean (4.24); (ii) the sensitivity all-12-capital sum peaks at BCE 1400 (14th c. BCE), again in the same window (driven additionally by daggers, depots and house size); (iii) no earlier century — including the amber peak (BCE ~3000) or the monument-only peak (BCE 2700, 2.96) — exceeds it. Therefore, the summed social capital peaked around 1300–1400 BCE.

payload.hypothesis: Summed social capital (Copper&Gold ZCU_AU + Amber Zamber + Monument Count ZMonument) peaked in the 14th-13th centuries BCE, exact maximum at BCE 1400 and 1300 (sum = 4.24 Z-units). At this peak the increasing components are Copper & Gold (record-high zone, +2.54) and Monument Count (+1.71, above baseline and rising +0.36 vs previous century); Amber is not elevated at the peak (-0.01, far below its BCE ~3000-3300 maximum). Independent interpolated-1yr cross-check and all-12 sensitivity sum both confirm the same 14th-century-BCE window.
payload.workflow: 1) Parse capital.csv (comma decimals) -> 39 century rows BCE 4300-500. 2) Verify each component is Z-standardized (mean~0, std~1) to justify equal weighting. 3) Primary index: per-century sum of ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument -> peak BCE 1400/1300 (4.238), 2nd place BCE 1100/1200 (3.622), distinct 3rd BCE 2700 (2.959). 4) Component assessment at peak: value vs own long-run mean and local change vs preceding century (above-baseline and/or positive-change flags). 5) Cross-check on time_series_data.csv interpolated columns (century means, 100yr/c): top = 14th c. BCE (4.24). 6) Sensitivity: all-12 sum peaks BCE 1400 (14th c. BCE); 3-mean peaks BCE 1300. 7) Synthesized data-grounded hypothesis. Script: analysis_social_capital.py; outputs: social_capital_series.csv, analysis_summary.txt.
